(By Pankaja B.C., Advocate.)
 JUDGMENT

The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/ for the injuries suffered by him in a road accident dated 24.05.2021.
2.

The case of the Petitioner in brief is that:
On 24.05.2021 at about 02.15 p.m., when the petitioner was proceeding in his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA04EU2001 to go to Kudaluru to Solur at NH 74,
Nelamangala Hassan Road, in front of Nandini Dairy Bus Stop a Car bearing Reg.No.KA09P6580 came with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner,
endangering SCCH-25 human life and dashed the petitioner's motorcycle from back side.
As a result petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was shifted to J.P. Hospital, Bangalore and he was an inpatient for 5 days in the said hospital.
He was aged about 26 years at the time of accident.
So far he has spent Rs.2,00,000/ towards conveyance, food and nourishment charges.

Prior to the date of accident he was hale and healthy, working as a Helper in the H.P.Gas, Solur,
Magadi Taluk, Bangalore, earning Rs.20,000/ per month.
Due to accidental injuries he has lost the income and future prospective life.
The Kudur Police have registered the case in Cr.No.137/2021 punishable u/Sec.279, 337 of IPC against the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA09P6580.
The 1st respondent being the RC owner and the 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence this petition.
SCCH-25 3. In response to notice issued by this Tribunal, the Respondents appeared through their respective counsels and filed separate written statements.
4. Objection of the Respondent No.1.
He has denied all the averments made in the petition.
He has admitted that the driver of the said offending Car has valid driving license as on the date of accident and the policy also is in existence.

Further he has denied the manner of accident, age, income,
avocation of the petitioner and contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence prays for dismissal of the petition.
5. Objection of the Respondent No.2.
It has denied all the averments of the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of policy in respect of the offending Car.
Further stated that the petition is bad for non joinder of necessary and proper parties.
The person riding the SCCH-25 vehicle has no relation in force.
The driver of the Car did not have valid and effective DL as on the date of accident.
The petition is not maintainable for non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of the MV Act.

Respondent Shivakumara.K.P vs Mahesh S.S on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185619813/
2 No.2 denied the involvement of the offending Car, the age, income, occupation of the petitioner and stated that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against them.
6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:

1 . Whether the petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 31.12.2022 at 9.30am,
due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA09P 6580 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
SCCH-25 2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3. What order or Award?
7.
The Petitioner in order to prove his case, has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.13.
On the other side, the Respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents.
8. Heard the arguments and perused the materials on record.

9. On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows: Issue No.1: In the affirmative, Issue No.2: In the affirmative, Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following: SCCH-25 REASONS 10. Issue No.1: In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA09P6580, the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 by reiterating the petition averments in his chief examination affidavit and produced 6 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.6.
During his crossexamination he has admitted that the accident road was a one way and the Car hit him from behind.
The dairy at Kudur cross was placed at the side of the road coming from Kunigal to Nelamangala.

Except this nothing worthwhile is elicited to show the absence of negligence on the part of the driver of the Car.
11.
The accident occurred on 24.05.2021 and the FIR was registered on the same day on the complaint of the petitioner's uncle.
The Mahazar was conducted on 25.05.2021 from 10.00am to 11.00am at Ex.P.3.
The SCCH-25 Wound Certificate at Ex.P.4 shows that the petitioner has suffered injuries on his left frontal and right temporal aspect which is grievous in nature.

The IMV report at Ex.P.5 shows the damages to the petitioner's vehicle at front wheel and mudguard, front fork, head light and indicator assembly, handle bar, both side body, all foot rest, rear wheel and mudgaurd,
seat damaged, rear suspension, tail lamp & indicator and fuel Tank damaged.
And the Car was also damaged to its front wind screen glass, engine bonnet, front bumper, left side head light and indicator, front left side fender and front left side door.
The police have filed the charge sheet after investigation as per Ex.P.6.

The Respondent No.2 has contended that the accident occurred due to Shivakumara.K.P vs Mahesh S.S on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185619813/
3
sole negligence of the petitioner himself.
But in order to prove the same they have neither produced any documents nor examined any witness.

Therefore, on the basis of the evidence of PW.1 and the documents before the court Exs.P.1 to P.6, the Tribunal holds that the accident occurred due to the negligence of SCCH-25 the driver of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA09P 6580.

Accordingly,
issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:
The Petitioner has further averred that on account of the accident he is suffering from grievous injuries.

The Petitioner to substantiate that there is loss of income due to the accidental injuries and that he is suffering from permanent disability has not examined either the treated Doctor or any other Doctor who has got expertise in this field.
He also has not placed any disability certificate issued by the competent person to prove that he suffered permanent disability.

Therefore, in absence of evidence this Tribunal holds that the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident has not caused him permanent disability resulting in loss of income and accordingly the version of the petitioner in this regard is not acceptable.
Under these circumstances the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income due SCCH-25 to disability.
However, it is pertinent to note that, the wound certificate produced as per Ex.P.4 discloses that, he has sustained grievous injuries.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/ under the head of Pain and Suffering.
The Petitioner has stated that he has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/ medical, conveyance and nourishment expenses.
In this regard he has produced 72 medical bills for Rs.90,946/ as per Ex.P.9.
There is no contrary evidence to this document from the respondents.
As such, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.90,946/ under the head of medical expenses.

As mentioned above the Petitioner was treated at J.P.Hospital,
Nelamangala, wherein he was treated for 8 days.
In this regard he has produced discharge summary of J.P. Hospital at Ex.P.7.
During that time, certainly he would have spent some amount towards attendant, conveyance, transportation and for other incidental expenses.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/ towards attendant, SCCH-25 conveyance, transportation and other incidental expenses.
The total compensation comes to Rs.1,40,946/.
If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.1,41,000/.
13. LIABILITY:
As discussed above the Respondents have failed to prove their defence about the accident.
Therefore, the Respondents Nos.1 & 2 being the RC owner and the Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.5,00,000/ but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.1,41,000/ alongwith interest @ 6% per annum.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is held in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.3:
For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following: SCCH-25 ORDER
The petition is allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,41,000/. (Rupees One Lakh Forty One Thousand only) along with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount by the respondent.

The Respondent Nos.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay Shivakumara.K.P vs Mahesh S.S on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185619813/
4 compensation to the petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within sixty days from the date of this award.
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner through epayment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per Rules.
SCCH-25 Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw decree accordingly.
(Typed to my dictation directly on the computer by the Stenographer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court on this the 15th day of March 2024)
